subject: Game Theory
title: Multi-Unit Auctions
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Multi-Unit Auctions.

hook.text: When selling many identical units—Treasury bonds, electricity, carbon credits—auction design gets complex.

buildup.text: Should all winners pay the same price (uniform) or each pay their own bid (discriminatory)?

discovery.text: Uniform pricing encourages aggressive bidding. Discriminatory pricing rewards cautious bidders.

twist.text: The US Treasury switched from discriminatory to uniform pricing in 1998. Revenue increased.

climax.text: Electricity markets use multi-unit auctions every few minutes to match supply with demand in real time.

punchline.text: One format doesn't fit all markets.

quiz.question: What did the US Treasury gain by switching to uniform pricing?
